You grade a first-hour triage against what the operator's own incident review later concluded.

For each finding, decide whether a duty team following the triage (its matched rules, next actions and escalation) would have been pointed at the substance of that finding during the incident:
- "yes": the triage names it or directs the action it describes.
- "partly": the triage points in the right direction but misses the key specific (the mechanism, the order, the threshold, the person).
- "no": nothing in the triage leads there.
For remediation findings (longer-term fixes), "yes" means the triage already applies that practice.

"by" lists the rule ids that earned the credit (empty for "no"). "note" is one short sentence. Judge only from the triage given; do not reward actions the triage did not state.

Reply with JSON only: {"per_finding":[{"finding":"F1","anticipated":"yes|partly|no","by":["R-001"],"note":"..."}]}

{"triage":{"classification":"recurring","matched_rules":[{"rule_id":"R-003","because":"The datacenter control system was in the process of failing away from one of its control hosts, which is the exact 'when' condition for R-003.","signals":["AWS-NRT-2019:S22"]},{"rule_id":"R-004","because":"The control system is unavailable (minimum visibility) and cooling did not transition to maximum cooling or purge mode in part of the datacenter, matching R-004's 'when' conditions.","signals":["AWS-NRT-2019:S26","AWS-NRT-2019:S28","AWS-NRT-2019:S30"]},{"rule_id":"R-002","because":"Mechanical cooling is down (cooling system shut down) and servers have begun shutting down due to overheating, indicating the thermal buffer is depleting and automated shutdowns have started.","signals":["AWS-NRT-2019:S26","AWS-NRT-2019:S3"]}],"next_actions":[{"action":"Manually investigate the affected cooling equipment, check the PLCs controlling the air handling units, reset affected equipment and PLCs into maximum cooling configuration, and confirm cooling is restored and temperatures are falling before standing down.","rule_id":"R-004"},{"action":"Treat the failover as a period of elevated risk to cooling availability, watch the cooling plant directly, expect that a fault in control system logic can make the control system unresponsive, and verify that cooling systems have actually entered their designed maximum-cooling fallback.","rule_id":"R-003"},{"action":"Treat the thermal buffer as a finite resource and act before it is depleted; expect that once the buffer is gone, temperature will exceed safe operational thresholds and automated device shutdown will begin, and recognize that in parts of the datacenter temperature can rise so quickly that hardware is damaged before it can shut down.","rule_id":"R-002"}],"escalate":{"now":true,"to":"incident commander","reason":"Thermal buffer depletion is imminent or automated shutdowns have started (EC2 servers shutting down due to overheating), and the control system failover is in progress with cooling not transitioning to maximum cooling or purge in part of the datacenter."},"not_covered":[]},"findings":[{"id":"F1","kind":"root_cause","text":"Due to a bug in the third-party control system logic, this exchange resulted in excessive interactions between the control system and the devices in the datacenter which ultimately resulted in the control system becoming unresponsive."},{"id":"F2","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"While this worked correctly in most of the datacenter, in a small portion of the datacenter, the cooling system did not correctly transition to this safe cooling configuration and instead shut down."},{"id":"F3","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"It was the failure of these PLC controllers which prevented the default cooling and “purge” mode from correctly working."},{"id":"F4","kind":"contributing_factor","text":"Because the datacenter control system was unavailable, the operations team had minimum visibility into the health and state of the datacenter cooling systems."},{"id":"F5","kind":"response","text":"To recover, the team had to manually investigate and reset all of the affected pieces of equipment and put them into a maximum cooling configuration."},{"id":"F6","kind":"remediation","text":"In the interim, we have disabled the failover mode that triggered this bug on our control systems to ensure we do not have a recurrence of this issue."},{"id":"F7","kind":"remediation","text":"We have also trained our local operations teams to quickly identify and remediate this situation if it were to recur, and we are confident that we could reset the system before seeing any customer impact if a similar situation was to occur for any reason."},{"id":"F8","kind":"remediation","text":"Finally, we are working to modify the way that we control the impacted air handling units to ensure that “purge mode” is able to bypass the PLC controllers completely."},{"id":"F9","kind":"impact","text":"It took longer to recover these instances and volumes and some needed to be retired as a result of failures to the underlying hardware."}]}
